title: clamp from its reference page
description:
Write your own `clamp` using only what its cppreference page says, then compare with `std::clamp`.

```
clamp(5, 1, 10) = 5
clamp(-3, 1, 10) = 1
clamp(42, 1, 10) = 10
matches std::clamp for 1000 random values: yes
```
hints: The page says "If `lo` is greater than `hi`, the behavior is undefined", which is the precondition to `assert(!(hi < lo))` (lesson 1.04).
It also says it uses `<` only, so write the comparisons with `<` and not `>`.
requirements: Read the page for `std::clamp` and copy its precondition into a comment.
Check the precondition with `assert` (it says the behaviour is undefined otherwise).
Return a reference like the real one does.
stretch: Add the overload that takes a comparison function, as the page lists it.
